$comment: Payloads that must be refused. A schema that accepts everything passes a suite of valid examples, so each of these isolates one rule the schemas exist to enforce.

cases.name: results: unknown schema version
cases.because: An unknown version means the sender believes something about this payload that the receiver does not. Refuse; never fall back to the newest known version.

cases.name: results: check_id is not a ULID
cases.because: The hub's idempotency and the prober's cursor both depend on check_id being sortable. A UUID would break ordered replay silently.

cases.name: results: timestamp with an offset instead of Z
cases.because: Both implementations claim to handle ISO-8601 and would still disagree. One form only.

cases.name: results: monitor_id as an integer
cases.because: Ids are strings on the wire. An integer here is the PHP/TypeScript mismatch this rule exists to prevent.

cases.name: manifest: heartbeat without an interval
cases.because: A heartbeat with no interval can never be judged late, so it would sit in the manifest doing nothing.

cases.name: manifest: event carrying heartbeat fields
cases.because: An event is judged by timeout, a heartbeat by interval + grace. Accepting both on one declaration leaves it ambiguous which rule applies.

cases.name: manifest: monitor interval of zero
cases.because: Zero would mean 'always due', which is a way to bill a tenant for a denial of service against their own site.

cases.name: manifest: non-HTTP monitor url
cases.because: The prober performs HTTP checks. Anything else is a request to make it fetch something it has no business fetching.

cases.name: heartbeat-verdicts: unknown status
cases.because: The hub maps each status onto one of its own events. An unmapped status would be dropped on the floor.

cases.name: results: unexpected field
cases.because: additionalProperties is false throughout, so a field one side invented and the other ignores is caught at the boundary rather than becoming an undocumented contract.
